identity.title: Maternal Foxh1 loss reduces locus-specific H3K27me3 and disrupts lineage segregation.

content.abstract: Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) establishes H3K27me3 marks to shape spatiotemporal gene expression during embryogenesis. How PRC2 is recruited to specific genomic loci remains debated, with a prevailing model favoring intrinsic chromatin affinity over recruitment by sequence-specific transcription factors. Here, we show that the maternally deposited pioneer transcription factor Foxh1 promotes PRC2 occupancy at specific genomic loci during zygotic genome activation in Xenopus. Foxh1 is a crucial mediator of Nodal signaling that pre-binds mesendodermal enhancers before signaling activation, facilitating enhanceosome assembly and coordinated mesendodermal gene expression in cooperation with other maternal transcription factors. Using maternal Foxh1-null embryos, we demonstrate that Foxh1 is also required for efficient Ezh2/PRC2 occupancy at a subset of Foxh1-bound loci. Loss of Foxh1 selectively reduces Ezh2 occupancy and associated H3K27me3 at these regions without substantially altering total Ezh2 levels. These findings support a dual-function model in which Foxh1 activates endodermal gene expression in endoderm, while promoting PRC2-associated repression of the same regulatory program in ectoderm. Thus, Foxh1 contributes to establishing spatially distinct epigenetic states that coordinate germ layer specification and lineage segregation during early embryogenesis.
